newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-LACK OF INTEREST DISAPPOINTS AMERICAN FED CUPPERS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LACK OF INTEREST DISAPPOINTS AMERICAN FED CUPPERS.

text.p: The U.S. Fed Cup team had been counting on wildly enthusiastic home support on Saturday.
As it turned out, they did not need it, but the embarrassingly sparse attendance was a huge disappointment.
"I really was very surprised today when we walked in -- whoa!, said Monica Seles of the sight of completely empty sections throughout the Atlantic City Convention Centre.
Organisers would not give attendance figures, but fewer than 2,000 turned out at the centre which could have held some 9,000.

Thanks to wins by Seles and Lindsay Davenport over Conchita Martinez and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, the Americans took a 2-0 lead in the best-of-five event even without the kind of support their opponents routinely receive as Fed Cup hosts.
"When we played in Nagoya we had 12,000 screaming fans, 11,000 were all against us, so it's a much different atmosphere here," Seles said of the July semifinal tie in Japan.
Before the final, the players and U.S. Captain Billie Jean King often spoke in anticipation of a packed partisan crowd.

After Saturday's play, the talk was of a thorough lack of Fed Cup awareness and the failure to properly promote the event in this gambling city, where the slot machine section of any casino had far more filled seats than the historic old Convention Centre.
"We wish more people would come out. I don't know if there are enough tennis fans in the city," lamented Seles.
"When you come to Atlantic City you don't come for tennis," she surmised.
"So few people know what's going on that when I would be walking at the hotel people would be saying 'Why are you here?' And I would be the one telling people why we were here.
"I don't think that's ever happened," she said.

Officials from Caesars Hotel, which promoted the event, said obscure International Tennis Federation rules had forbidden them from using the names of the players until only recently, when the teams were announced.
And posters that say only "Fed Cup, U.S. vs Spain" without marquee names like Seles, Sanchez Vicario, Davenport and Martinez just do not sell the event.
"It feels quiet. You know we had 6,000 people packed in in Valencia," said King, comparing Saturday's showing to last year's final in Spain.
"People in the United States don't know what Fed Cup is. I think we need more exposure. I think we have a lot more promoting to do."
The difference was not lost on the Spanish stars, who are regularly supported by thousands of extremely vocal, flag-waving fans.
"There's not much people here," noted Martinez. "The atmosphere is really different because when we played in Valencia everybody was rooting for us.
"There was a lot more people in Valencia than over here."
Davenport tried hard to find a silver lining.
"I was disappointed there weren't more people here," she said. "But they did seem to really understand what was happening."
